data.name: Joachima
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Joachima means 'Jehovah adds'. In the Bible, Joachima is the name of a woman from the Old Testament who made a vow to God and was miraculously answered. This name is associated with devotion, faith, and the power of God's intervention.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes faith, devotion, and God's intervention.
data.numerology_meaning: A nurturing and loving soul, who feels the need to help others. Loyal, caring, and generous, with a great sense of responsibility and duty.

in_hebrew.name: יואכימה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יואכימה הוא שם עברי שמקורו בשם יהויקים, שפירושו 'ה' יקים' או 'ה' מכין'. בשורש העברי, השם יואכימה קשור למילה 'עקמ' שפירושו 'להקים' או 'להכין'. השם יואכימה הוא שם נשי שמקורו מהשם הגברי יהויקים, ומשמעותו היא 'אלהים יקים ומכינה האדמה' או 'ה' מכין ומקים את האדמה'.

in_greek.name: Ιωαχίμα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιωαχίμα είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יהויקים (Yehoyakim), που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός θα υψώσει' ή 'Ο Θεός θα αναστήσει'. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Ιωαχίμα συνδέεται με την έννοια της ανύψωσης και της αποκατάστασης. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και χρησιμοποιήθηκε για να εκφράσει την ελπίδα και την προσδοκία για την έλευση του Μεσσία.

in_latin.name: Joachima
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Joachima derivatum est ex nomine hebraeo יהויקים (Yehoyakim), quod significat 'Deus suscitabit' vel 'Deus exaltabit'. In traditione christiana, nomen Joachima saepe coniungitur cum idea resurrectionis et exaltationis. Nomen hoc a primo Christianis adoptatum est ut spem et expectationem adventus Christi exprimeret.

in_english.name: Joachima
in_english.meaning: God will raise or God will establish
in_english.long_meaning: The name Joachima originates from the Hebrew name יהויקים (Yehoyakim), which means 'God will raise' or 'God will establish'. This name has been adopted in various Christian traditions and is associated with the concept of divine elevation and restoration. Historically, the name Joachima has been used to express hope and expectation for the coming of the Messiah. In Christian tradition, the name Joachima symbolizes spiritual growth and divine support.

saint_reference.note: Joachim was the father of the Virgin Mary and is considered a saint in the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, and Anglican traditions.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joachima has a rich cultural history, particularly in European Christian tradition. In Spain, Portugal, and other parts of the world with a heavy influence of the Catholic faith, there are churches and shrines dedicated to Saint Joachima, the mother of Mary, the mother of Jesus. The story of Saint Joachima is often portrayed in art and literature as an example of faith and dedication to God.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Joachima holds deep spiritual significance in Christianity. It symbolizes the idea that God adds to our lives in profound ways. The Old Testament story of Joachima serves as a reminder that God hears and answers prayers, and that faith and dedication to Him can bring about miraculous results. The name is also a reminder of the importance of making and keeping vows to God, as Joachima did when she vowed to consecrate her son to His service. Overall, the name Joachima inspires a sense of faith, devotion, and trust in God's capacity to bring about blessings in our lives.

historical_references.reference:
Joachim was the name of a biblical figure from the Old Testament who was the husband of Saint Anne, the mother of the Virgin Mary. According to tradition, Joachim and Anne were childless for many years despite their deep desire for a child. They both made a vow to God that if He granted them a child, they would dedicate the child to His service.
After praying fervently, Anne became pregnant and gave birth to the Virgin Mary. In some versions of the legend, Joachim is said to have been visited by an angel who told him to go to the temple to offer a sacrifice on the day his wife would give birth. When he arrived, he encountered Anne and their baby, who were also at the temple. He was overjoyed and gave thanks to God for answering their prayers.
Time period: Before the birth of Christ (approximately 1st century BC).
Context: Christian tradition.

Another reference to Joachim comes from the Middle Ages, specifically the 13th century, when a German mystic named Joachim of Fiore predicted the coming of three ages of the Holy Spirit: the Age of the Father, the Age of the Son, and the Age of the Holy Spirit. Joachim believed that the last age would be marked by the appearance of a new and perfect human being, who would bring about the end of the world and the Second Coming of Christ.
Time period: 13th century.
Context: Christian mysticism.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Joachima' is increasingly being recognized in modern contexts beyond its traditional religious context as a saint. On religious apps and websites, Joachima is mentioned alongside other Christian saints and their stories, offering spiritual guidance and inspiration. Social media platforms like Twitter and Instagram are seeing an uptick in hashtags related to 'Joachima' and feminist spirituality, as women seek to reclaim and reinterpret the stories of traditional saints through a modern, feminist lens. Interfaith dialogue groups, both online and offline, are also discussing Joachima's legacy and how it can be applied to interfaith contexts. Overall, Joachima's name is being used as a symbol of female strength, resilience, and the power of spirituality to transcend tradition and inspire change.
